questions.question: What are the os package's file operations in Go?
questions.title: Os Open Create Readfile
questions.direct_answer: os.ReadFile(name) → []byte, os.WriteFile(name, data, perms), os.Open(name) → *File (read), os.Create(name) → *File (write). The simple forms handle the whole file; the File forms give streaming control.

sections.title: Quick Revision
sections.content: os.ReadFile(name) → []byte, os.WriteFile(name, data, perms), os.Open(name) → *File (read), os.Create(name) → *File (write). The simple forms handle the whole file; the File forms give streaming control.

sections.title: Interview Answer
sections.content:
The forms, executed:

```go
// WriteFile — simple write
os.WriteFile("/tmp/test.txt", []byte("content"), 0644)

// ReadFile — simple read
data, _ := os.ReadFile("/tmp/test.txt")
// data == "content" — verified

// Open + manual control (streaming, offset)
f, _ := os.Open("/tmp/test.txt")
defer f.Close()           // ALWAYS
buf := make([]byte, 100)
n, _ := f.Read(buf)       // n bytes actually read

// Create + write
f2, _ := os.Create("/tmp/out.txt")
defer f2.Close()
f2.WriteString("written")

// Remove
os.Remove("/tmp/out.txt")
```

When to use which: ReadFile/WriteFile for small-to-medium files (they load/save the whole thing — one call, no lifecycle). Open/Create + Read/Write + Close for: large files (streaming in chunks), seeking (ReadAt/Seek), appending (OpenFile with O_APPEND), concurrent-position access.

The Close discipline: EVERY Open/Create must have a deferred Close — the OS file descriptor is a resource; the GC doesn't close it deterministically. defer f.Close() at acquisition is the pattern that eliminates the leak class.

The permission bits: 0644 (owner read/write, others read) for data files; 0755 for executables; 0600 for secrets. These are the same bits as chmod.

sections.title: Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    RF[ReadFile: whole file] --> B[]byte]
    OP[Open: streaming] --> F[File] --> R[Read chunks] --> C[Close]
    CR[Create: write] --> F2[File] --> W[Write/WriteAt] --> C2[Close]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
The ReadFile vs Open+Read trade: ReadFile makes ONE allocation for the whole file (size known or grown via ReadAll internally) — the whole thing in memory. For a multi-GB file, that's a crash — the streaming form (Open + a fixed-size Read loop) is the only option. The interview honesty: ReadFile is the RIGHT default for code, configs, small data; streaming is the necessary exception for big inputs.

The File.Write + buffering relationship: direct os.File writes are unbuffered syscalls (each Write is a system call). For many small writes, wrap in bufio.NewWriter(f) — buffer, then Flush. The composition: os.Create for the file + bufio.Writer for batching + defer both Flush and Close — the three-layer idiom every Go file-writing code uses.

The atomic-write pattern (the production trick): write to a temp file, then rename (os.Rename) over the target. Rename is atomic on most filesystems — the reader never sees a half-written file. os.CreateTemp + write + rename is the crash-safe save.
